From: Avery Foster <avery@lumos.ai>

Date: 2028-09-08T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up on pricing after today's demo

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Theo and I found the latency and the autoscaling behavior really promising. A couple of items procurement asked me to clarify so we can move this forward:

- Expected monthly token burn (our current internal estimate): 30M tokens/month baseline, with growth to ~80M/month in Q4 if the pilot goes well.
- Peak TPS we need to plan for: sustained 15 TPS for normal operation; we see short bursts up to ~220 TPS for ~1-3 minute windows during heavy user events.
- Token mix: roughly 70% user input (short prompts ~50-150 tokens) and 30% generation (avg 350 tokens).
- Budget target: our procurement target is around $700-$1,000 per 1M tokens depending on SLA/commit terms; they asked whether we have a committed/discounted option and what minimums look like.

Can you send a short options table (pay-as-you-go vs commit bands) and confirm whether Hosted API can handle the short 220 TPS bursts without moving to Dedicated? Also, what test plan would you recommend so we can validate peak behavior before committing?

Appreciate the quick reply — we want to lock a PoC timeframe for mid-October if possible.

Best,
Avery Foster
VP Product, Lumos AI
Avery | lumos.ai

Hi Avery / Theo,

Thanks — great to be aligned on volume shape. Short answers up front: Hosted API can support the scenario you described (sustained ~15 TPS with short 220 TPS bursts) with the right burst/band configuration; you do not strictly need Dedicated for short spikes, though Dedicated gives stronger latency SLAs for sustained high QPS.

Attached is a concise options sheet (redwood_hosted_pricing_v1.pdf) — high level summary below so procurement has something to circulate quickly:

1) Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
   - Unit price: $1,000 per 1M tokens
   - No minimums; includes automatic prefix caching and standard burst allowances

2) 6-month committed band (20% off)
   - Unit price: $800 per 1M tokens
   - Recommended commit band: 40M - 100M tokens/month (slab pricing with overage at pay-as-you-go rate)

3) 12-month committed + burst cushion (30% off)
   - Unit price: $700 per 1M tokens
   - Commitment: 60M tokens/month minimum; includes guaranteed burst allowance up to 250 TPS for short windows (policy-based)

Notes and clarifying Qs:
- The unit prices above are for text-generation workloads with the token mix you described. Embeddings or heavy reranking would be priced separately.
- To size burst handling on Hosted: we configure a dedicated burst pool per-customer + auto-fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained. For your 220 TPS spikes, plan to include a short 5–15 minute burst cushion in the PoC to stress the autoscaler.
- Can you confirm the % of requests with function/tool-calls or external tool latency? That affects token turnaround and pipeline concurrency.

Next steps I propose:
- You fill & return the attached token profile spreadsheet (lumos_token_profile_draft.xlsx) with 7-day sample traces if available.
- We schedule a 60-minute PoC load window where we ramp to your 220 TPS spike (we handle the test harness).
- After the PoC we issue a formal pricing proposal and a recommended commit band based on observed effective tokens and latency.

If you'd like a one-off introductory flexibility (smaller initial commit + option to scale), I can loop in Sales Ops for an approved bridge discount.

Will you be able to share sample traces by EOD next Wednesday? That would let us book capacity for the mid-Oct PoC.

Cheers,

— Soojin Lee
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Lumos' estimates and my initial banding. Quick asks:

- Can we approve the 12-month committed band at $700/1M with a guaranteed short-burst cushion up to 250 TPS? Lumos is explicitly asking for pricing in the $700–$1,000 range and has a clear mid-term growth profile.
- Revenue math: using current Lumos estimates (baseline 30M -> 80M in Q4), the ARR range at $700/1M is roughly $252k -> $672k annually (not including potential overages). If they take 12-month commit at 60M/mo = $504k ARR.
- Risk: they may ask for a temporary lower commitment while the PoC completes — can we allow a 3-month ramp clause with prorated commit?

I included my proposed guardrails in the attached pricing PDF. Also need Ops confirmation we can provision a burst pool that will reliably absorb 220 TPS spikes for their PoC window without moving them to Dedicated. Karthik — can you confirm capacity constraints and whether a short-term burst pool of ~1k vcores equivalent is feasible in us-west for mid-Oct?

Thanks,
Soogin (typo fixed) — Soojin

Avery / Theo,

Following up with a consolidated proposal after internal alignment. Thanks for sending the draft token profile — that helped tighten the bands. Summary below and next steps so procurement and engineering have a short checklist.

Pricing summary (hosted API) — generation-focused text workload
- Option A — PAYG (no commit): $1,000 / 1M tokens
- Option B — 6-mo commit (recommended entry band): $800 / 1M tokens; recommended commit 40M–100M/mo; overage billed at PAYG
- Option C — 12-mo commit + burst cushion: $700 / 1M tokens; 60M/mo minimum; includes built-in burst allowance up to 250 TPS for short windows and priority autoscaling for production events

What this means for Lumos (based on your 30M -> 80M projection):
- If you choose Option B at an initial 40M/mo commitment and scale to 80M/mo by Q4, your effective blended price falls between $800–$1,000/1M during ramp, with predictable monthly invoices.
- Option C gives the best unit economics at scale; we can add a 3-month ramp clause that allows a 50% reduction on the first quarter of committed qty to reduce PoC risk — we typically require a signed SOW for that flexibility.

Technical/operational notes:
- Hosted can handle your sustained 15 TPS baseline automatically. For the 220 TPS spikes we recommend a 5–15 minute PoC ramp (we'll provision a temporary burst pool). If PoC shows sustained >120 TPS beyond those short windows we recommend Dedicated.
- We'll run a controlled PoC load test mid-Oct (you indicated that timeline). Please confirm an exact 2-hour window and provide 7-day sample traces if available.

Requested next steps (short checklist):
1) Lumos: return the completed lumos_token_profile_draft.xlsx with sample traces (or the seven-day sample)
2) Redwood: reserve mid-Oct PoC slot and share test plan + harness details
3) Lumos: indicate preferred pricing option (A/B/C) and whether you want the 3-month ramp clause included
4) Redwood & Lumos: finalize SOW + sign to lock committed band and burst cushion (if Option B/C)

I'm copying Marissa (sales lead) and Karthik (capacity/ops) for any contractual or capacity questions. If you prefer, I can also run a short call with procurement to walk through the numbers this week.

Would you like the SOW template and sample PoC schedule now or after you send the traces?

Thanks — looking forward to the PoC.

Best,
